outline: How AI can generate realistic fake content
Risks of deepfake audio, video, and images
Importance of source verification and media literacy

slides.title: Learning Objectives Slide
slides.narration:
In this tutorial, you will learn,

• Define misinformation and deepfakes.
• Explain how **AI** generates fake content.
• Identify risks associated with deepfake technology.
• Apply strategies for source verification and media literacy.

No coding needed.
slides.image_prompt: Pre-requisite Slide

slides.title: Understanding AI-Generated Fake Content
slides.narration:
Let's look at **AI** generated fake content.
**AI** can create convincing fake content.
slides.image_prompt: Section Header: Understanding AI-Generated Fake Content

slides.title: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs)
slides.narration:
What are **GANs**?
**GANs** are a primary technology. They generate fake media. They learn to create new data.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration showing GANs with simple icons

slides.title: Deep Learning for Synthesis
slides.narration:
How does deep learning work?
Algorithms are trained. They synthesize realistic audio. They also create video and images.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration showing deep learning algorithms synthesizing audio, video, images

slides.title: Types of AI-Generated Content
slides.narration:
What types of fake content exist?
**AI** can produce fake news articles. It can create virtual influencers. Many forms of fake content are possible.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration showing various types of AI-generated content like fake news, virtual influencers

slides.title: The Dangers of Deepfakes
slides.narration:
Now, let's move to the dangers of deepfakes.
Deepfake technology has significant risks. It also has negative impacts.
slides.image_prompt: Section Header: The Dangers of Deepfakes

slides.title: Impact on Trust and Credibility
slides.narration:
How do deepfakes affect trust?
They erode public trust. Trust in media is lost. Trust in information sources is also lost.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration showing broken public trust, media, and information sources

slides.title: Manipulating Individuals and Narratives
slides.narration:
Deepfakes can manipulate opinions.
They spread disinformation. They can damage reputations. They affect individuals and narratives.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration showing manipulation of opinions, disinformation, and damaged reputations

slides.title: Legal and Ethical Implications
slides.narration:
What are the legal issues?
Deepfakes pose legal challenges. They create ethical dilemmas. Proliferation of deepfakes is a concern.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration showing legal scales and ethical dilemmas related to deepfakes

slides.title: Deepfakes in the Real World
slides.narration:
Let's look at deepfakes in the real world.
We will explore actual instances. We will see societal consequences.
slides.image_prompt: Section Header: Deepfakes in the Real World

slides.title: Political Manipulation Examples
slides.narration:
How are deepfakes used politically?
They influence political discourse. They impact elections. This can manipulate public opinion.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration showing political figures, voting booths, and manipulated public opinion

slides.title: Financial Fraud Examples
slides.narration:
Deepfakes are used in fraud.
They are employed in scams. They cause financial deception. Think about it.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration showing financial fraud, scams, and money deception

slides.title: Damage to Reputation
slides.narration:
Deepfakes can damage reputations.
They discredit public figures. They also target private citizens. This has serious consequences.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration showing a damaged reputation, discrediting public figures, and targeting private citizens

slides.title: Vague Example: A Misleading Audio Clip
slides.narration:
Open any **AI** tool.
Type this in the message box. Ask for a misleading audio clip.
Click **Submit**.
Notice the quality. Is this clear or vague?
slides.image_prompt: Screen close-up: user typing 'Ask for a misleading audio clip...'; AI generating response on screen

slides.title: Improved Example: Analyzing a Convincing Deepfake
slides.narration:
Let's improve it.
Type for a convincing deepfake. Ask for realistic features. 
Click **Submit**.
See how it could fool viewers. Compare this to the last example.
slides.image_prompt: Screen close-up: user typing 'Ask for a convincing deepfake...'; AI generating response on screen

slides.title: Comparison: Real vs. Deepfake Features
slides.narration:
Compare the outputs.
We will visually compare real media. We will compare it with a deepfake. Notice the subtle tells. See the difference?
slides.image_prompt: Side-by-side: real media vs deepfake output, highlighting subtle differences

slides.title: Combating Misinformation: Your Role
slides.narration:
Now, let's look at combating misinformation.
We will discuss your role. You can identify deepfakes. You can counter misinformation.
slides.image_prompt: Section Header: Combating Misinformation: Your Role

slides.title: Techniques for Source Verification
slides.narration:
How can you verify sources?
Use reverse image search. Cross-reference information. Check metadata carefully.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration showing icons for reverse image search, cross-referencing, and metadata check

slides.title: Developing Critical Thinking Skills
slides.narration:
Develop critical thinking skills.
Question all information. Evaluate the evidence. Consider any biases.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration showing a person with a thought bubble, questioning information, and evaluating evidence

slides.title: Tools and Resources for Detection
slides.narration:
What tools can help?
Many online tools exist. Use fact-checking websites. Browser extensions are also useful.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration showing icons for online tools, fact-checking websites, and browser extensions

slides.title: Promoting Media Literacy
slides.narration:
Promote media literacy.
It is a broader concept. It creates an informed society. This is very important.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration showing media literacy promoting an informed society

slides.title: Summary Slide
slides.narration:
Let us summarize what we learned.
We defined misinformation and deepfakes. We explored how **AI** generates fake content. We also discussed the risks. We learned strategies for verification and media literacy.
slides.image_prompt: Summary Slide

slides.narration:
Now as an assignment,
find two news articles. One real and one deepfake. Compare the results.
